title: One-Apartment World Model
evidence:
REFUTED on the model, confirmed on the splat half.

1) SANA-WM training is CUDA-only at the kernel level. NVlabs/Sana `pyproject.toml` pins `triton==3.5.1`, `flash-linear-attention>=0.4.2`, `xformers==0.0.33.post2`, `bitsandbytes`, `mmcv==1.7.2`; `environment_setup.sh` installs torch/torchvision from `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128`, `conda install -c nvidia cuda-toolkit=12.8`, and `flash-attn>=2.7.0 --no-build-isolation`. None of these have an Apple Silicon build.

2) The released SANA-WM Stage-1 recipe is 8-GPU minimum: `torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 train_video_scripts/train_sana_wm_stage1.py --config_path configs/sana_wm/stage1/sana_wm_stage1_sekai_chunk_causal_cp2_fsdp2.yaml` — FSDP2 + context-parallel 2. The config's attention type is literally `ChunkCausalGDNTriton`. Pre-training is stated as "15 days on 64 H100s". The gated-DeltaNet kernel comes from flash-linear-attention, whose README says "verified on NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel hardware" (CUDA/ROCm/XPU/NPU/CPU) — no Apple, no Metal, and no pure-PyTorch training fallback. Triton has no Metal backend, so both the forward and the backward of the model's core attention are missing on this machine.

3) The one Apple Silicon implementation is inference-only. github.com/AasthaShayla/sana-wm-mlx (4 stars, last updated July) describes itself as "a from-scratch MLX port of the full inference stack" — no training, no LoRA training, no backward pass. Its hand-written Metal gated-DeltaNet scan is forward-only, so it cannot be differentiated even in principle without writing a VJP.

4) Its benchmark is on the user's exact machine and kills the demo. M4 Max 128 GB: "36.4 s per step", 40 steps ≈ 24 min for a 10.1 s / 161-frame 704×1280 clip, 40 GB peak; "an RTX class GPU ... is still roughly 10x faster at this workload". 30 steps was tested and rejected ("degrades"). So the concept's "sana-wm-mlx serving frames to the browser at ~1-2 fps" is off by 3-4 orders of magnitude, and there is no distilled few-step causal checkpoint in the port to close that gap.

5) The fallback is also not a training path. lpalbou/mlx-gen is inference-only with LoRA *loading*, not LoRA training ("LoRA support is route-specific ... adapters trained externally"). Its own Wan2.2 A14B numbers: 152.7 s for 384×224×33f T2V on an M5 Max. There is no MLX or MPS LoRA trainer for any video diffusion model; mflux trains images only (Z-Image, FLUX.2 Klein).

6) The user's own repo already reached this conclusion. /Users/changkeun-jobis/Documents/private_projects/sml-lab/docs/vision-ideas-2026H2.md:120 lists SANA-WM in the table "멋지지만 지금은 안 되는 것" with the blocker "xformers, flash-linear-attention". /Users/changkeun-jobis/Documents/private_projects/sml-lab/docs/models-2026H2.md:75: video models "MPS에서 추론은 되지만 분 단위. 학습은 대상 아님."

7) What DOES check out: splat-local (COLMAP or Depth Anything 3 on MPS → Brush Rust/Metal trainer → PLY/SPZ/SOG) measures 13 m 22 s end to end for an 11-second walkthrough, 200 frames @ 2048px, 18k steps, on Apple Silicon. Spark loads ".PLY (also compressed), .SPZ, .SPLAT, .KSPLAT, .SOG" and is driven by a normal three.js WebGLRenderer + camera. So the ground-truth half of the demo is real and mac-native. Brush's offline render-from-poses is NOT documented (README only documents train/view/load; crates/brush-cli/src/main.rs is a 404), so the "headless render with known poses" step has to be built, not invoked.
tooling:
Claimed but nonexistent: there is no Apple Silicon training path for SANA-WM. sana-wm-mlx = inference only; NVlabs/Sana training = torchrun 8×GPU + FSDP2 + Triton/xformers/flash-attn.

What actually trains on this Mac, and does the job:
- 3DGS: `splat-local` (wraps Brush, Rust/Metal trainer) or `metal-gauss` — verified mac-native, ~14 min per short clip.
- Headless render rig: Playwright + Chromium + Spark 2.x on a three.js `WebGLRenderer` with scripted camera poses and `readPixels` (must be written; ~150 lines).
- The trainable model: `third_party/minRF` already vendored at /Users/changkeun-jobis/Documents/private_projects/sml-lab/third_party/minRF/{dit.py,rf.py} — port to MLX, train an ~80-120M camera-conditioned next-frame rectified-flow DiT from scratch.
- Optional photoreal layer: `mflux` LoRA training on Z-Image 6B (Apache-2.0, official mflux training support per /Users/changkeun-jobis/Documents/private_projects/sml-lab/docs/models-2026H2.md:66).
- Captioning: CapRL-Qwen3VL-2B (MLX). Browser: ONNX export → q8/q4f16 → Transformers.js v4 / ORT Web WebGPU. Divergence metric: dinov3-vits16 ONNX.
data_reality:
Three separate problems.

(a) The capture is the wrong shape. splat-local's own guidance is "Avoid moving subjects, whip pans, and textureless walls"; "move slowly in an orbit/arc with lots of overlap; end near where you started (loop closure)"; and "COLMAP scales superlinearly with frame count". Its measured 14 min is for an 11-second clip at 200 frames. A single 15-minute multi-room walkthrough is ~80× the footage and is precisely the documented failure case: white walls, doorway transitions, no loop closure between rooms. Expect hours of COLMAP and a real chance of a split or broken reconstruction, not "1-2 h". Fix: 8-12 short clips of 25-40 s, one per room plus one per doorway transition, each an arc that returns to its start; reconstruct per-clip and merge, and use the Depth Anything 3 pose path for textureless rooms.

(b) 6,000 clips is not 6,000 examples. 96,000 frames resampled from one splat is one scene with a camera schedule. A rank-64 LoRA over a 2.6B video DiT on a single scene memorizes the splat's floaters, popping and view-dependent SH artifacts as the texture prior; the 300 real snippets (~0.3% of the corpus by frame count) will not counterbalance that. If you want the model to learn the floor plan rather than the renderer, the render distribution has to be the training signal (action-conditioned next-frame), not free-running clips.

(c) The camera action format is not public. The SANA-WM doc describes "Dual-Branch Camera Control ... per-frame trajectory adherence (6 DoF)" but gives no tensor spec; only the redistributable Sekai-Game camera data is released ("~235 GB ... 961 frames, 16 fps, 640-pixel overlap") and the doc notes "the internal training curriculum also mixed separate video-only and no-camera data sources". Converting his splat poses into that action space is reverse-engineering with no reference implementation.

Licensing: the apartment footage is his own, fine. SANA code is Apache-2.0 but the `Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-WM_chunk_causal` checkpoint license must be checked per file — his own repo's lesson #3 (docs/vision-ideas-2026H2.md) is exactly that bundled weights can carry a different license than the repo.
memory_gb_estimate: Memory is not why this fails — worth stating plainly so it isn't the thing that gets "fixed". SANA-WM LoRA as specified: 2.6B bf16 weights 5.2 GB + rank-64 adapter and Adam states <1 GB + LTX-2 VAE and text encoder ~4 GB + checkpointed activations at 480p/16f roughly 15-35 GB = ~25-45 GB peak, comfortably inside 110 GB. The plan's "~55 GB" is a guess but not wrong in kind. For reference, sana-wm-mlx inference at 704×1280×161f measures 40 GB. Corrected plan: <20 GB peak for the from-scratch ~100M DiT at batch 32 / 128px; Brush splat training ~8-16 GB; optional mflux Z-Image 6B LoRA ~30-40 GB.
hours_estimate:
As written: not reachable at any hour budget. Before step 1 you must write a differentiable chunked gated-delta-rule kernel in MLX (custom Metal kernel plus VJP), a training loop, a latent/VAE encode pipeline and a camera-token encoder against an unpublished spec — 80-200 h of research porting with no convergence guarantee, versus the claimed ~10 h.

The arithmetic in the plan is, notably, not the problem: scaling the measured 36.4 s/step by the ~16× token reduction from 704×1280×161f (~18.5k tokens) down to 480p×16f (~1.2k tokens) gives ~2.3 s forward, ~7-9 s for forward+backward, so 3,000 steps ≈ 6-8 h. That is exactly why the plan reads as plausible. The FLOPs are fine; the kernels do not exist.

Corrected plan, wall clock: ~4 h capture + per-room splats (12 clips × ~14 min, parallel with capture), ~2 h to build the Playwright/Spark render rig, ~1 h to render 200k frames, 8-9 h unattended overnight MLX training, ~4 h ONNX export + WebGPU page. One weekend, ~19 h of which ~9 h is the machine running alone. Optional Z-Image LoRA adds one more overnight (~6 h).
corrected_plan:
Keep the idea, throw away the base model. The honest version is stronger anyway: don't LoRA someone else's world model on one apartment — train your own world model that has only ever seen one home, small enough to run in the visitor's browser. That also lands squarely on sml-lab's actual thesis (갈래 C) instead of streaming frames off the Mac.

Stage 0 — capture (Sat morning, ~4 h). 8-12 clips of 25-40 s: one slow arc per room, one per doorway transition, each ending where it started. Run splat-local per clip (COLMAP default; Depth Anything 3 MPS pose path for the white-wall rooms), merge into one scene, export .SOG + .PLY. Measured basis: 13 m 22 s for 200 frames @2048px, 18k Brush steps.

Stage 1 — build the render rig (Sat afternoon, ~2 h + 1 h render). Playwright + headless Chromium + Spark on a three.js WebGLRenderer, offscreen 256×256, readPixels to PNG. Derive a floor-plan occupancy grid by projecting splat opacity onto the floor plane, then walk collision-free trajectories using the *exact WASD action set*: 6 discrete actions (forward/back 0.15 m, strafe 0.15 m, turn ±15°). Emit tuples (frames t-1,t | action | frame t+1). 60 fps offscreen gives 150k-250k tuples in under an hour. Separately keep ~2,000 real phone frames with their COLMAP poses as an honesty/eval set the model never trains on.

Stage 2 — train the world model from scratch, overnight (8-9 h). Port third_party/minRF (dit.py + rf.py, already in the repo) to MLX. ~80-120M-param DiT, 128×128 RGB (or train a tiny 8× autoencoder first in ~1 h and work in its latent). Conditioning: two previous frames channel-concatenated + a 6-way action embedding + a learned pose-derived room token. Rectified flow, logit-normal time sampling, batch 32, bf16. Cost check: 6·N·T ≈ 6·1e8·256 ≈ 1.5e11 FLOPs/sample; at ~8 TFLOPS effective (25% MFU of 34) that is ~0.02 s/sample, ~0.6 s/step at bs 32, so 50k steps ≈ 8-9 h unattended. Peak memory <20 GB. Mix in the real frames at ~10% with an "is_real" flag so the model doesn't fully inherit splat floaters. This is the piece that is genuinely trained, genuinely yours, and genuinely only ever saw one apartment.

Stage 3 — ship it into the page (Sun, ~4 h). Export to ONNX, quantize q8/q4f16 (~100 MB for 100M params — inside the repo's own "2 GB after click" budget), run under Transformers.js v4 / ORT Web on WebGPU. 8 flow steps × ~1.5e10 FLOPs at ~1-2 TFLOPS in-browser ≈ 0.1-0.2 s/frame → 5-10 dreamed fps in the *visitor's* browser. No WebSocket, no Mac in the loop, works when the Studio is asleep.

Stage 4 — /flat, the demo. Split screen: left is Spark rendering the real splat at 60 fps (ground truth), right is the dream model, both driven by the same WASD keys from the same starting photo. Divergence is measured, not asserted: dinov3-vits16 ONNX in the browser embeds both views each step, and the cosine distance is painted onto the floor plan as a live heat map — "where the model gets lost" becomes a number. Visitors can save a dream trajectory and rate it.

Stage 5 — optional second weekend, the photoreal hallucination shot. mflux LoRA on Z-Image 6B (Apache-2.0, official mflux training support) over ~1,200 splat renders + real frames, captioned by CapRL-Qwen3VL-2B with room name and heading. Not interactive video — a "dream still" button: stand in the hallway, press it, and the LoRA paints the room that isn't there at 1024px in 20-40 s. Overnight, mac-native, and it is the actual wow image for the blog post.

Dropped entirely: SANA-WM, sana-wm-mlx, the Wan2.2 LoRA fallback, and WebSocket frame streaming.
notes:
The single most decisive fact is that the only Apple Silicon SANA-WM implementation is a forward-only inference port, and its own measured 36.4 s/step on this exact machine already invalidates the interactive demo even if training were somehow solved. The concept's risk section names "unsupported MPS ops" as the top risk, which understates it by a lot: it is not a few missing ops, it is that the model's attention kernel (ChunkCausalGDNTriton, via flash-linear-attention) exists only as Triton, and its named fallback (Wan2.2 LoRA in mlx-gen) is also inference-only.

Two salvageable ideas from the original that I kept: the side-by-side ground-truth splat vs. model dream, and the "where does it get lost" heat map — both survive intact and get *better* when the dream model is small enough to run client-side. The rated-divergence page is a natural artifact with viewer state if he wants it.
